sections.h2: Choosing a route in New Berlin
sections.html:
New Berlin homeowners can use an agent, run the sale personally, or take a cash buyer's offer that comes with no repair demands. Work needed on the house and your move-out date tip the decision. Whatever you pick, the state requirements further down still apply.

  • Agent listing. This gives the widest exposure, though buyers commonly request inspections and repair credits. The listing agreement sets the commission. See the percentage and all other charges on paper before signing.
  • Private sale. You take on advertising, showings and paperwork, including the condition report and deed.
  • Cash offer. Financing and repairs usually drop out. Check the contract for the closing date, the party paying for title work and any fee subtracted from your proceeds.

Eastern Waukesha County holds New Berlin, a Milwaukee-area city of 39,953 people. Owners live in about 76.5 percent of homes, and 23.6 percent of residents are 65 or older. Many houses have been in one family for years and show it in layers of renovation. For those, gather permit history early, because a buyer's inspector may want to match kitchens, decks and furnaces to permit records.

A median owner-occupied value of $365,700 comes from a survey of every owner-occupied home. What yours sells for depends on its condition, its lot and when you list.

sections.h2: School districts and your tax bill
sections.html:
Four districts serve the city between them: Elmbrook, Muskego-Norway, New Berlin, and West Allis-West Milwaukee. The Schools page on the city's site lists all four and the private schools.

Your tax rate depends on which district your parcel is in. The city's Tax Levies and Rates page breaks out each one. Find the district on your own bill first, because parents shopping for a home usually ask about it before anything else.

Community Development, on the second floor of City Hall at 3805 S. Casper Drive, is the place to begin. Permit applications are accepted Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 4:00 pm. Inspectors cover the front counter from 8:00 to 9:00 am on weekdays, and reviewing a building permit may take up to 10 business days.

A buyer's inspector may compare the following kinds of past work with permit records.

  • New or replacement furnaces, air conditioners and water heaters
  • Decks, whether attached or detached, plus garages, sheds and similar accessory buildings
  • Kitchen remodels, additions, alterations and recreation rooms
  • Generators, hot tubs, pools and solar panels
  • Razing of a structure

If you cannot tell whether earlier work had a permit, phone Community Development before you list.

Water, sewer and stormwater bills also surface at closing. Wis. Stat. 66.0809 adds a 10 percent penalty to a utility balance still open after October 31, and a balance plus penalty can move onto the tax bill after November 15. Pay off anything outstanding before the sale. For the dates of the yearly notice, Open Book and Board of Review, ask the assessor's office.

Wis. Stat. 709.02 applies to homes of one to four units. You prepare a Real Estate Condition Report, and the buyer has to get it by day 10 after acceptance. A late report gives the buyer a way out: two business days after day 10 to rescind and recover deposits.

The report is a disclosure and promises nothing about the house. Court-appointed fiduciaries who never lived there are excused by Wis. Stat. 709.01, and so are transfers exempt from the transfer fee. Suppose you learn something after finishing the report but before the buyer accepts. Wis. Stat. 709.035 then asks for an amended report within 10 days of acceptance. Fill in every line, since an unanswered item leaves the report incomplete.

On top of recording, the seller owes a state transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value (Wis. Stat. 77.22). The register collects it when the deed arrives. Waukesha County's fee guide says to round the price up to the next hundred before figuring it. Recording itself is $30 at the Waukesha County Register of Deeds.

Certain transfers owe no fee. Section 77.25 names transfers by will, descent or survivorship, along with a foreclosure deed or deed in lieu to a mortgage holder. After a spouse dies, use the HT-110 form. The county wants no tax bill or death certificate with it.

sections.h2: What happens after you accept an offer
sections.html:
Here is how the weeks usually go. Acceptance sets the condition report clock at 10 days. Within that stretch you complete the report, settle the water, sewer and stormwater payoff and have your title company or attorney draft the deed, parcel number included. The transfer return is filed online, and its receipt goes with the deed to the county, accompanied by a check or money order covering recording and any state fee.

Cash buyers trim the start of this timeline, since no appraisal or loan approval sits between acceptance and closing. The report, return and recording all stay.

Pull together what a title company will ask for before buyers start calling. Your tax bill gives the parcel number. Your lender supplies a payoff figure. Add permit records for earlier work, the name of your school district, and water, sewer and stormwater account details so the last bill closes out cleanly. When a deceased spouse is still on title, include the HT-110 form, a transfer return receipt and a copy of the document showing the interest.

Next, have every buyer or agent answer the same three questions in writing: when will we close, what fees come out of my proceeds, and what happens if the inspection finds a problem. Written answers make offers easy to compare. Keep every quote, because a cash buyer's figure and an agent's net after commission only line up when both are on paper.

faqs.q: Can I sell my New Berlin house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, ask for it in the contract. Many cash buyers work that way. You still owe a condition report unless an exemption fits, due within 10 days of acceptance.

faqs.q: Who covers the transfer fee in a New Berlin sale?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor, at 30 cents per $100 of value under Wis. Stat. 77.22. The register collects it at recording, and any other closing charges are for the contract to settle.

faqs.q: How long until I get my recorded deed back from Waukesha County?
faqs.a: Immediately for an e-recorded deed. A paper deed comes back right away if you gave a valid email address, or in two to three weeks by mail with a stamped return envelope.

faqs.q: What paperwork follows a co-owner's death?
faqs.a: File form HT-110 with a transfer return receipt, a copy of the document showing the decedent's interest and a $30 check or money order. Confirm details with the office or an attorney.

faqs.q: Do unpaid utility bills affect a New Berlin sale?
faqs.a: They can. A balance open after October 31 takes a 10 percent penalty, and the balance plus penalty may move onto the tax bill after November 15. Pay water, sewer and stormwater charges before closing.
